skill.name: next-dev-loop
skill.description: Verify Next.js changes in a running development app using framework diagnostics and a real browser.
skill.summary: Cross-check compilation, runtime errors, visible behavior, and React state after Next.js edits.
skill.author: vercel

security_audit.summary: Of 74 static findings, 72 are false positives involving Markdown, ordinary diagnostics, documentation links, or local development access. Two findings confirm instructions to install an unpinned global package without an explicit approval step; a separate concern is retained authentication state without cleanup guidance. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious reconnaissance, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:47-49 directs installation of agent-browser@latest when the CLI is missing, without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before installation, pin a reviewed compatible version, and prefer a project-local dependency over a global installation.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:71-74 and 195-198 persist login cookies and browser storage without retention or deletion guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose authentication persistence, use dedicated test accounts, and document storage protection and explicit state deletion when retention is unnecessary.

content.user_title: Verify Next.js Changes in a Running App
content.value_statement: Successful builds do not prove that a Next.js change works in the browser. This skill cross-checks framework diagnostics, visible behavior, and React state during development.
actual_capabilities: Check framework version, Turbopack availability, and required MCP tools before verification.
Use runtime route metadata to identify the files involved in a page.
Check compilation issues and framework-reported runtime errors after edits.
Drive a real browser to verify navigation, interactions, and visible outcomes.
Inspect React component trees, props, state, and render counts with React DevTools enabled.
Reuse worktree-scoped browser sessions and recover from stale session state.
limitations: Requires a running Next.js development server, Next.js 16.3 or later, and Turbopack.
Requires agent-browser 0.31.1 or later and a working Chrome environment.
Does not replace production testing or support a weaker fallback when prerequisites fail.
Browser sessions retain authentication state; the skill provides no state-deletion procedure.

use_cases.title: Validate Interface Changes
use_cases.description: Check that a changed page compiles, renders without errors, and responds correctly to user interaction.

use_cases.title: Investigate React Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare visible behavior with component state and render counts to investigate unexpected updates or suspense behavior.

use_cases.title: Verify Reported Browser Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce a reported navigation problem and distinguish application errors from stale or misdirected browser sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Check Development Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my running Next.js app meets this skill's prerequisites. Report missing requirements and ask before installing or upgrading anything.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Page Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify my latest edit to [route]. Check compilation, runtime errors, and visible behavior in the running app.

prompt_templates.title: Test an Authenticated Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [interaction] on [route] using a dedicated test account. Keep the browser session worktree-scoped and confirm authentication-state retention with me.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: verify behavior with authenticated browser state.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a React Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [regression] on [route] using framework diagnostics and React introspection. Reconcile browser state, inspect render behavior, and verify the fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: investigate behavior across framework and browser observations.

output_examples.input: Verify a successful save after changing the profile page.
output: Runtime: no framework-reported errors after navigation.
Browser: saving displayed the updated profile value.
React: component state matched the visible value.

output_examples.input: Check why a route appears blank after an edit.
output: Framework diagnostics reported no compilation issues.
The browser session returned an empty snapshot.
Reopening the same session restored the expected page.
The observed failure came from stale browser state, not the edited route.

output_examples.input: Verify the app when the required browser CLI is missing.
output: Verification stopped because agent-browser was unavailable.
The workflow requires agent-browser 0.31.1 or later.
Runtime behavior remains unverified until the required browser tooling is available.

best_practices: Confirm the actual development port and required tool versions before testing.
Use a dedicated test account and explicitly agree on authentication-state retention.
Preserve active development output and use separate ports for production tests.
anti_patterns: Treating a successful build or type check as proof of correct browser behavior.
Deleting active development output or running production tests against the development server's port.
Installing unpinned global tooling without review or keeping sensitive login state on shared machines.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Which Next.js setup is required?
faq.answer: The instructions require Next.js 16.3 or later, Turbopack, and a running development server.

faq.question: Does the skill start the development server?
faq.answer: A running development server is a prerequisite. The instructions leave it running after verification.

faq.question: Why does it use both MCP and a browser?
faq.answer: Framework diagnostics expose compilation and runtime context. The browser verifies visible behavior, interactions, and React state.

faq.question: Does it preserve login state?
faq.answer: Yes. Worktree-scoped sessions restore saved cookies and local storage, then save state when closed.

faq.question: Does this replace production testing?
faq.answer: No. The workflow checks development behavior and recommends separate output and ports when running production tests.
